findings.message: Section 20 grants only 'Exit ... reads only the committed report before authoring Phase 5 core'. Unlike the Phase 3 and Phase 4 boundary registries, it gives no Phase 5 core registry: no seed stems, owning modules, fences, tiers, depends edges or Context partition. The only such partition is in section 19's Phase 4 Emits (line 1497): retro stage plus drain-invoker hook, then retro-to-box activation, then `phase5-continue`, as three single-seed admissions. The ticket does not cite section 19, and section 20 itself records that full section 19 cannot be rendered within the 160,000-char bound. The acceptance criteria require the test to pin 'ownership, dependency, Context, bounded-render, and finite-registry closure' and reject an 'off-registry Phase 5 payload', but no registry in the render defines what is on-registry. The implementer would have to invent the Phase 5 seeds.
findings.paved_road: fix the plan, then re-author the ticket

findings.message: Section 19's Phase 4 exit reads (line 1497) require these report members: failover onto the fixture candidate, proven by served-identity stamps; a soft-band spiral notification fired exactly once; a hard-timeout kill with a harvested run; and a persisted cooldown Timer with its matching `timer_fired`. The merged closed schema RELIABILITY_BATTERY_MEMBERS is exactly (classified_quota_exhaustion, all_candidates_cooling_recovery, unclassified_failure_preservation), and its report file is also named differently from section 19's `reliability-report.json`. Section 20 does not say whether validating this merged schema satisfies the Phase 4 exit. As written, the exit either closes Phase 4 without evidence section 19 requires, or it can never go green.
